decisions.note: Round 3 prototype offered no way to fix a garbled auto-title/summary; client asked for inline rename before maker had surfaced it.
Round 3 prototype actually created a second copy when the same URL was pasted twice; client rejected the duplicate outright.
Round 4: clicking title text always opened the page, making the rename control (hidden pencil) practically undiscoverable; client rejected this as landing 'on the wrong side'.
Round 5: of A/B/C rename mechanisms, client selected 'C' (Edit panel) specifically because it can grow to hold tags/note/url edits per full REF-BM-04 scope.
Round 7: labels only supported single-pile filtering; client asked for combined 'work AND still-to-read' filtering, a capability never surfaced.
Round 8: multi-word search required exact phrase order ('remote office' found nothing); client supplied the correct rule (loose AND by default, quotes for exact match).
Round 11: page-preservation/snapshot was never surfaced across the whole 'trust' narrative; client raised the dead-link decay risk unprompted-in-substance.
Round 12: maker's snapshot answer didn't address the PDF sub-rule; client added the requirement to keep the actual PDF file, not a wrapper snapshot.
Round 13: maker's 'final scope' recap silently dropped the previously agreed note field; client caught the omission and had it reinstated.
Round 13: import of existing bookmarks was entirely absent from the presented 'complete' scope; client flagged it as make-or-break and it was added before build.
Round 13: export of the collection was entirely absent from the presented scope; client required it before agreeing to cross over to real build.
Round 13: alternate sort orders (oldest/name) were never presented as part of the scope; client requested them and they were added in round 14.

Round 15: folder-to-label import created case-sensitive duplicates ('Work' vs 'work'), violating the tag-uniqueness behavior already established for manual entry; client supplied the case-insensitive merge fix.
Round 15: nested browser folders ('Recipes > Italian') collapsed to only the innermost label, losing the outer folder; client corrected it to keep both levels as labels.
Round 15: export produced bare links with no labels/notes, undermining 'not locked in' trust promise; client required labels (as folders) and notes to ride along.
